source.title: Rethinking generalization of classifiers in separable classes scenarios and over-parameterized regimes
source.authors: Julius Martinetz; C. Linse; T. Martinetz

record.file_problem: None; the supplied text contains the full paper and appendix.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses random-label generalization and cites prior work for it, but its own experiments use true labels and vary training-set size. They do not test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper states that random labeling can yield zero training error with chance-level generalization, but attributes this to cited work [4]. Its own results concern generalization on true labels. Theoretical statements about random labeling are not experiments on the paper's own results.
record.test_reason: The experiments bear on V5's true-label clause: networks trained without weight decay or data augmentation achieve zero training error and good generalization, particularly the ResNets. Random-label fitting is cited and assumed in the theoretical illustration, rather than tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors relate generalization to the density of classifiers by true error and obtain reasonably fitting learning curves, with deviations especially at small sample sizes and for MLPs. Their faster-learning conclusion concerns sample requirements, not optimization time.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies true-label generalization as training sample size varies and proposes a density-of-classifiers model; it does not reproduce random-label experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, architecture, and training-sample count affect the reported test-error curves; the paper notes model-fit deviations, particularly at small n and for MLPs.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger ResNets have smaller fitted asymptotic errors and require fewer samples to approach them; larger MLPs do not share the latter advantage.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture affects generalization as training-set size increases among interpolating classifiers.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Network (2024); Version of Record presented at IJCNN, DOI stated in text.
record.problems: The paper does not experimentally test random labels or label-noise fractions. Test-error values are presented in figures, while the text gives only qualitative descriptions; runs vary in training samples and initial weights.
record.rows_left_out: No separate row was created for each training-sample count because the figure-only values are not recoverable from the supplied text. Fig. 4 and Fig. 5 show mean test errors and standard deviations across the sweep; the aggregate trend is represented per model and dataset.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting by standard deep networks, unchanged training settings, and accompanying chance test error.
Optimization time for true versus random labels and convergence across corruption fractions. Faster convergence with sample count is a different measure.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian inputs.
Training and test error across label-corruption fractions.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting; separate effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation; matched comparisons quantifying the effect of removing each.
Temporal ordering of learning real patterns and memorizing noise.

record.verdict_notes: Section 3.1 derives chance error for random labels conditional on its density model and zero-training-error premise; it does not independently establish random-label trainability.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting, chance test error, and whether architecture or hyperparameters must change.
Training-time comparison and convergence as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled, permuted, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test error across a sweep of label-corruption fractions.
Effects of explicit regularization on fitting random labels and true-label generalization.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: ResNet018
rows.operation_detail: Trained to zero training error on true-label MNIST subsets; test error measured across training-set sizes.

conditions.value: 10 to 60000; specific results shown in Fig. 4

rows.measure: Mean test error and standard deviation across runs
rows.value: The networks converge quickly to very small test errors; figure reports results by sample size.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviations over 50 runs are shown; exact values not stated in text.
rows.note: True labels; the paper reports the result in a figure and describes the trend in text. Does not test the listed claim versions.
rows.check: The link to V5 was missed. At sufficiently large training-set sizes, MNIST generalization is good without weight decay or augmentation. The small-n results do not establish good generalization throughout the sweep.
